question: Why did the first answer of this incident arrive malformed? The engine path that engages only for long contexts is the sparse indexer's selection, and the checkpoint declares a recency guarantee it has to keep.

checkpoint_declares.source: the served checkpoint's config.json; engine/profiles/glm53/facts.py asserts all three

incident_boot.how_checked: git cat-file -p fd99f82e:engine/profiles/glm53/net.py | grep -c pin -> 2, both 'typing' and 'skipping'; engine/modules/sparse_indexer.py at that commit has no tail_pin_pools and no pin_pools_in_logits
incident_boot.what_the_docstring_said: engine/modules/sparse_indexer.py at that commit still promised '(`index_kpool_always_select_tail`: the newest tokens are always attended)'

negative_control.how: extract engine/modules/sparse_indexer.py from fd99f82e into a scratch package and import the pin from it
negative_control.reading: the function this request needed did not exist on the boot that served it; PR #1159 added it ten hours later

fix.what: tail_pin_pools names the pool that just completed and pin_pools_in_logits raises it above the row's own maximum before the top-k, in prefill and in the captured decode path (_select_rows reads the lengths it already had)
fix.its_test: tests/test_engine_tail_pin.py names the lengths 50004 and 50005 and counts tail_pin.would_have_been_dropped

trigger.rule: the appended tail covers [pool_len * pool_size, seq) and is EMPTY when seq % kpool == 0
trigger.reading: on those steps the newest complete pool had to win the relevance top-k like any older pool; when it lost, the selection carried none of its tokens and the appended tail - empty there by construction - could not put them back

open_measurement.what: how often the newest pool actually lost the indexer's top-k during this request's decode, i.e. the frequency of the harm on this prompt
open_measurement.why_unmeasured: engine/modules/selection_capture.py records only the first PREFILL selection per layer (its docstring says the selection is 'the 2026-09-17 incident's last unverified path'), and no selection-*.pt exists under the fleet's dumps
open_measurement.instrument: arm ST_SELECTION_CAPTURE on a boot, extend the capture to the decode steps at whole-pool lengths, then read tail_pin.would_have_been_dropped from tools/selection_reference.py over those dumps
open_measurement.what_it_would_not_prove: a frequency is not a text: the effect on the visible answer still needs the pin-on/pin-off pair on the same prompt
